edges.title: A track of a philosophy becomes the goal; each phase names its framework
reads_from_source: tracks[] (ways to follow the philosophy; the builder picks one)
tracks[].phases[] (id, name, kind, weeks, framework_id, text)
phase rules the generator reads: priority_override, exclude_exercises, rotate_main_lifts, tests, week_templates, drop_order
track_for_level, then primary_track_id, then the first track
bias (else scope) — fallback priorities
training_contract.yaml — the track's contract, when the package has one
training_contract.yaml tracks.<id>.options — choices the athlete makes for the track, each with a default (Wildman's swing minutes); both builders ask
fidelity.yaml inventions — a track the app made up rather than the source is labelled in both builders
reads_from_target: expectations (ideal days and session minutes are read)
applicable_when + days_per_week — only for a goal whose phase names no framework
engine_decides: goals.philosophy_to_goal builds the synthetic goal (api._philosophy_to_goal wraps it; never shown to the user)
Track phases → phase timeline; every week runs the framework its phase names (phases.week_entry)
Phase kind (data/commons/phase_kinds.yaml) drives archetype filters, multipliers, cadence spreading and the deload reading
A legacy framework_id maps to the track and phase that run it (goals.owner_track_for_framework)
Priorities from the longest phase's framework sessions_per_week (the first wins a tie), else the bias
The goal carries the track's training contract; a blend drops it and composes lanes (src/composition.py)
The athlete's answers ride in the constraints as contract_options; an option left out, or a choice it does not offer, takes its default

edges.title: A training contract places its modules as written
reads_from_source: training_contract.yaml tracks.<track id>: modules (blocks, exposures a week, spacing, requires_mastery, optional, variants + rotation, periods, phases)
progression per module: density_cycle, timed_cycle, weekly_volume, load_per_exposure, ladder
implement, test_module, deload_phases, options (the athlete's choices, each with a default)
reads_from_target: the athlete's days, minutes, level, mastered exercises, implements, confirmed module state
engine_decides: Each week: the modules its phase runs, each at the step its confirmed sessions earned (a plan forecasts every exposure clean)

Every placement of the essential modules on the day pool is scored — closes a test week with its test, days shared with another track, modules stacked, optional work fitted, then spacing: same-modality days back to back, same-modality neighbours, body regions loaded heavily a day or two apart, the gap between each module's own sessions — and the best is taken
A module with periods deloads in its own deload period; otherwise the framework's frequency does
Optional work is offered by the last build week's minutes and never costs an essential session its day
A week whose required modules cannot fit is refused (ContractError), never trimmed; verify() refuses a program that breaks the phase's own claims
A slot is the module's block: no archetype is chosen and no exercise scored
constants: the placement search looks at up to 500 candidates

edges.title: A week template writes the source's week day by day
reads_from_source: the phase's week_templates: seven days per week of the phase — rest, a day category, several, or {categories, warm_up, light}
drop_order: which days go when the athlete trains fewer days
reads_from_target: the framework's categories: pools of named-workout archetypes (pool_only), each with a fallback order, long_day, advice; warm_up_category
each named workout's level, required_equipment, minutes and movements
engine_decides: The athlete keeps the template's days in order, dropping by drop_order; days keep their positions, honouring preferred and forced-rest days

Each day takes the next workout of its pool the athlete can do as written (level, every implement, every movement fillable, the day's minutes), passing one done in the last week while another fits; then the category's fallbacks
A warm-up from the warm-up pool opens the day when both fit; the two become one session
Loads are as written: the slot's load text, no ramp, level, phase or deload scaling
A day nothing fits is left out (a test may still take it); a program in which nothing fits is TEMPLATE_UNFILLED
constants: a workout counts as recent for the last week of picks (RECENT)

edges.title: The modality scheduler allocates sessions and assigns days
reads_from_source: synthetic_goal.priorities (modality weights)
phase_sequence[].priority_override — matched on the phase kind, so two phases of one kind share the first's
framework.sessions_per_week, allocation_mode, modality_priority (committed / core)
framework.cadence_options (rotating week to week)
framework.deload_protocol.frequency_weeks
framework.recovery.allow_consecutive (+ phases)
reads_from_target: priority_tier (kept when days are scarce), typical_duration_minutes
engine_decides: Largest-remainder rounding converts priority weights → integer session counts
_RECOVERY_COST_RANK {high:3, medium:2, low:1} — placement order; an unknown cost counts as low
Recovery windows: a modality's own recovery_hours_min (24 h without one); two high-cost modalities max(48 h, either's); checked both ways and against last week's end (_neighbours)
recovery.allow_consecutive lifts a pair whose window is 24 h or less
Days from cadence_options; a phase kind that spreads cadence takes the first pattern; _DEFAULT_SPREAD without one
Incompatibility: no two incompatible_in_session_with modalities share a day
Templated phases and training contracts place their own sessions — every shipped single-philosophy track
constants: Day scoring (+3, −6, ×1.25, −12 a session), allocation thresholds 0.8 / 0.7, 75 ideal minutes

edges.title: The scheduler's session picks its archetype by score
reads_from_source: modality id (primary filter)
recent sessions (the last 14 archetype ids, heavy body regions)
reads_from_target: pool_only / test-only — never picked by modality
modality fallback_rank, or the framework's fallback_modalities — the cross-modality fallback order
data/commons/constraints/category_equipment.yaml — the equipment each exercise category needs
engine_decides: Runs only for a session left to choose: template days, contract modules and tests are placed, not scored
Scoring: +6 full equipment, −3 if in the last 14, +3/−2 day fit, up to −8 injury impact, −10 per slot whose category the equipment blocks, +10 the preferred (split-day) archetype
Regional load: −2/−1 per body region a session a day/two days before loaded heavily, cap −4 (recovery_regions.yaml)
Ties: the least recently used, then the first authored
scaling.equipment_limited (or the generator's relaxed pass) lets an archetype past the equipment filter, without the +6
scaling.time_limited lets an over-long archetype through; with none fitting, the shortest is kept and trimmed to the session (populate_session)
No archetype for the phase: fall back in the framework's or the modalities' order (aerobic_base → durability → mobility), recorded as substituted_for
constants: Short-day cap 50 min (api TIME_MAP short 40 / long 75)

edges.title: A slot takes an exercise from its own package
reads_from_source: slot.slot_type
slot.exercise_filter: exercise_ids, ordered, movement_pattern, category, bilateral, equipment_required, exclude_movement_pattern, intensity
slot.intensity (heavy sets × reps make a main lift)
reads_from_target: data/commons/movement_patterns.yaml complements — what a complementary mobility block recovers
data/commons/training_levels.yaml — the level order, and the level that unlocks everything
data/commons/intensities.yaml — the intensities that make a main lift
engine_decides: Candidates: the goal's packages and those they borrow from (provenance), plus unattributed exercises; the whole library only under a non-strict policy
exercise_ids (in order when ordered), movement_pattern aliases (data/commons/movement_patterns.yaml) and category filter together
Level prerequisites: requires resolved transitively against data/commons/level_concepts.yaml and the package's level_seeds.yaml
Slot constraints: AMRAP / for_time slots reject skill, mobility and rehab; zone1–2 aerobic slots keep low effort; phase exclude_exercises
Scoring: −2 per recent use (last 40), +0.5 for unlocks (not in a slot that names its exercises), +0.5 for defined movement_patterns; ties to the first authored
Main lifts (heavy sets × reps) keep one exercise through a phase unless it rotate_main_lifts
A phase kind that excludes_max_effort (taper) drops effort: max exercises

edges.title: The progression model writes the load
reads_from_source: slot.slot_type
slot.sets / reps / intensity / rpe_target
slot.rest_sec, work_sec, time_cap_sec, hold_seconds
slot.duration_minutes / duration_sec
slot.distance_m
slot.scaling.intensity_pct / volume_multiplier
slot.load (as written), slot.standard (a test's scored slot)
slot.switch_at_sec, rest_until_hr_pct (watch cues)
block.alternate {exercise_id, when} — an EMOM block's even rounds another movement when the track's options say so
reads_from_target: exercise.category — only for the no-start-load note
data/commons/progression.yaml — RPE load factors and the weekly ramps (a framework's progression_defaults overrides them)
data/commons/training_levels.yaml — each level's share of a distance slot
data/commons/intensities.yaml — which intensities prescribe heart-rate zones, and their bands
engine_decides: Model (training_contract.resolve_model): the framework's progression_overrides for the modality, its own model when prescription_policy is framework, else the modality's, else linear_load
Dispatch by model and slot type
Time and distance ceilings: the phase kind's volume_multiplier (data/commons/phase_kinds.yaml)
Deload: deload_protocol.volume_reduction_pct is the share kept; a counts_as_deload kind's share is the total
as_written frameworks and a test's scored slot (standard_tests.protocol_load) are prescribed exactly as the source writes them

An alternating interval (Wildman's Option C): odd rounds the block's movement, even rounds its alternate if the athlete's equipment and injuries allow it; the load carries alternate, its note leads with it, and both watches title each round (alternateName)
constants: _DEFAULT_INCREMENT_KG 2.5 and the other defaults: 3 × 5, deload share 0.6, density 0.70 / 0.75, AMRAP 1200 s

edges.title: Several tracks compose one program
reads_from_source: lanes: [{philosophy_id, track_id, weight, start_phase}] — tracks of different methods, or two of one
each track's contract or week templates (a scheduler track cannot be composed)
reads_from_target: the athlete's days and minutes, shared by weight
engine_decides: Every track runs its own phases on its own engine; a week's own fields are the lead track's
Each week the contracts place first, lightest first, on the days each keeps (reserve_days); then the templates, each into the minutes the others left (day_room)
A placement avoids another track's days and a body region it loads heavily

A week that cannot fit gives way cheapest first, for the whole program: optional work, then one weekly session of the module with the fewest minutes, then the weekly volume — each cut a compromise naming its track; a cut that breaks a track's own phase rules is undone
A track that cannot run alone is refused as such at once

edges.title: A phase tests its standards
reads_from_source: the phase's tests: when (week: first | last | <n>, or every: <n>), a rotation of archetypes, in_place_of, on_deload
an archetype marked test:, each scored slot pointing at a standard
reads_from_target: the standard (the commons' or the package's standards.yaml), the athlete's level, equipment and minutes
engine_decides: The test takes the place of one session of the week — same day, same count — when the athlete can do it as written; else the week records tests_skipped with why
The session it stands in for is still selected, so the rest of the program is what it would have been, and is recorded as test.instead_of
A scored slot is prescribed as written (no ramp, level, phase or deload scaling); adjust and swap leave it alone
A training contract places its test in its test module's session
constants: a test fits when its minutes are within 1.1× the session's

edges.title: The athlete's constraints filter, and the program says what they held back
reads_from_source: equipment, injury_flags, training_level, days_per_week, session_time_minutes, mastered exercises
reads_from_target: an archetype's required_equipment and training_levels; an exercise's equipment, movement_patterns, contraindicated_with and requires
injury flags (the commons'; a package pattern's excluded_by joins them)
engine_decides: An injury flag excludes movement patterns and named exercises; a slot whose pattern is fully excluded is injury_skip
An exercise needs every implement it lists; prerequisites resolve transitively from the level's concepts and the package's level_seeds
An empty slot always says why (blocked_by); a session that stands in says so (substitution_cause)
The pre-flight check applies to scheduler and templated tracks; a contract refuses as it builds

edges.title: Which packages a caller sees, and what a package may add
reads_from_source: a package folder: philosophy, frameworks, archetypes, exercises; optional analytics, watch, contract, standards, vocabulary
reads_from_target: the shipped packages (data/packages) and, for the caller, their own overlay (user_packages)
engine_decides: The shipped root is everyone's and fail-fast; an overlay only adds — a shipped id keeps the shipped copy — and a package in it that does not load is set aside alone
A package may add modalities, movement patterns and equipment (vocabulary.yaml) and standards (standards.yaml), never an id the commons define
An athlete's package is installed only through every gate, its ids carrying the owner's prefix
Slot types, progression and contract models, phase kinds, levels, intensities, watch templates and icons stay the engine's

notes: No route; the file is written by hand or through the MCP server
src/phases.validate_philosophy_tracks checks track and phase ids (validate_entities.py)
PUT /api/frameworks/<id> ✅ — name, source_philosophy, sessions_per_week, cadence_options, deload_protocol, applicable_when, notes, recovery — custom package only
POST /api/modalities ✅ — the schema requires its display block, so the clients' generator can always read it
A package adds its own in vocabulary.yaml instead (roadmap 20.6)
POST, PUT, DELETE /api/archetypes ✅ — the custom package only (403 elsewhere)
slot_type is a schema enum, checked on create and edit
POST, PUT, DELETE /api/exercises ✅ — the custom package only (403 elsewhere)
Loads come from starting_load_kg / weekly_increment_kg / sessions_per_week; without them, generic defaults
No per-file route for analytics, watch, level_seeds, exercise_media, training_contract, fidelity, source_weeks, standards or vocabulary: a whole package goes through POST /api/packages

authoring.writes: user_packages (Postgres), laid out as the athlete's overlay
notes: POST /api/packages {files} ✅ — every gate with the owner's id prefix; dry_run checks only; 422 with the problems
GET /api/packages, /api/packages/<id>; DELETE (409 while the athlete's program is built from it)
Private to its owner; behind the authoring gate until the builder ships (roadmap 20.5)
mcp_server.py: write_package_file, validate_package, delete_package — local, inside the packages folder
Checks every file kind with the gates' own validator, and a package with add_package's checks (docs/mcp/README.md)
